caption: A sugar cube is dropped into a glass of hot water and another into a glass of cold water at the same moment, and the cube in hot water crumbles and vanishes first.

sa.check: Two glasses of water stand side by side, one hot and one cold.
A sugar cube is dropped into each at the same moment.
The cube in the hot water darkens, slumps and disappears.
The cube in the cold water is still a visible lump at that point.
Steam or ice shows which glass is which.

pc.expect: Each cube only shrinks and crumbles and neither grows back; the difference between them does not reverse.
pc.fail: A cube grows; or a crumbled cube gathers back into a whole cube; or the cube in the cold water disappears while the hot one is still a lump; or a cube alternates between larger and smaller.

pc.expect: Each cube goes by dissolving into its own glass; the sugar does not appear elsewhere or vanish at a stroke while whole.
pc.fail: A cube vanishes in a single frame while still square; or a third cube appears; or a cube passes through a glass's wall; or a cube moves from one glass to the other.

pc.expect: Both cubes fall downward into their glasses and sink to the bottom, and the sweet streams sink and spread.
pc.fail: A cube floats at the surface and stays; or a cube hangs motionless in mid-water; or a cube rises out of the water; or the streams climb out of the water.

pc.expect: Each cube is a pressed block of grains that wets, darkens and crumbles at its edges, and the water closes round it.
pc.fail: A cube stays dry and sharp-edged under the water; or a cube melts into a glossy liquid lump; or a cube bounces off the glass's floor like a ball; or the water holds a dent around a cube like a solid.

pc.expect: Two glasses and two cubes; the glasses keep their shapes and the cubes stay sugar as they crumble.
pc.fail: A glass changes shape; or a cube turns into another object; or a cube fuses with the glass's floor; or a glass vanishes.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The glasses' shapes, the table and the water's clarity stay the same.
pc.fail: A glass changes pattern; or the table's setting rearranges; or a glass's water turns a colour.
